messages:
oliver: Seeing memory climb on canary with long-context jobs. Two OOMs yesterday afternoon on shard-3 during a 32k run. Not sure if it's allocator fragmentation or our background shrinker not keeping up. Anyone able to run a quick reproduce? :thinking:
sasha: Can you paste the run args and the commit hash? might be easier to repro locally. :eyes:
oliver: repro command below + hash: `git@...:main#c4d2a1e`
```
run_bench --model redwood/13b --seq_len 32768 --concurrency 8 --requests 200 --enable-kv-cache
```
Also attaching the canary log snippet: `oom_kill: cgroup memory limit exceeded` and frequent `arena_alloc` failed traces in runtime logs.
jia: I can run this on a 3090 pool later tonight. Quick Q: do you want a heap profile or just /proc/meminfo sampling? I can do both.
kevin: If this is jemalloc-related, try enabling the background purge and junk flags. On previous fragmentation issues enabling `MALLOC_CONF: background_thread:true,lg_dirty_mult:1` lowered RSS spikes. Also run `jeprof` if you can get heap samples.
oliver: good call. canary has MALLOC_CONF unset currently. Trying to avoid global env flips on prod canaries; maybe we test on canary-dedicated first.

sasha: Another option is to enable the slab-shrinker debug sampling we added in runtime last month (`--shinker-sample-interval=10s --shinker-batch=64`) to see if the shrinker falls behind under sustained allocation churn. That will add logs but should be low risk.
emma: FYI I've got a PR open that touches the allocator hot path (https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/789). It adds an eager free for ephemeral arenas. If oliver's seeing regressions after that merge, ping me and I'll prioritize a revert or tweak. :slightly_smiling_face:

oliver: PR 789 is the exact change. Rolled to canary two days ago. Reverting would be quick but I'd prefer data first. jia, if you can run the bench with and without that PR on the same node that would be ideal.
jia: I'll run 3 variants tonight: base (pre-PR), pr-789, and pr-789 + jemalloc background_thread. Will collect heap profiles and `pmap`/`smaps` snapshots every 30s. Command I'm going to use: 
```
for tag in base pr789 pr789-bg; do 
  git checkout $tag && ./scripts/start_bench.sh --config longctx --out ./results/$tag.json &
  sleep 600
  pkill -f start_bench
  sleep 30
done
```
I'll upload logs to the run-results bucket and post links.
kevin: Also capture `/proc/vmstat` and `jemalloc.stats` after each run. If fragmentation grows but total allocated decreases, that's a strong signal for arena fragmentation.

infra-bot: Deploy canary pr-789 onto cluster:canary-3 started by ci-bot at 1782458800. Logs: https://ci.internal/build/4421 :gear:

sasha: If the sample interval for the shrinker shows it's not invoked often enough, we could add a burst-trigger that runs on high-rss transitions. But I'd like to see the logs first.
oliver: Agreed. jia — if you can also capture `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./runtime_binary ...` for a shorter run, that would help show hot allocation callsites. No need for super long perf runs.
jia: noted. Will do perf for first 120s of each run.
emma: I'll queue a quick code-review of a minimal revert branch so we can flip it fast if ci shows regressions. Linking the revert branch here: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/branches/revert-789

oliver: Thanks. One more ask: if this repros only under kv-cache heavy workloads, mention that — might be related to our KV cache growth + ephemeral allocations (prefix caching + per-request buffers).
kevin: Right. If kv-cache is the trigger we should test with `--kv-cache=off` vs `on` and measure working set. Also ensure `--kv-shared=true` vs `false` for canary.
sasha: I'll add a small instrumentation addition to log kv-cache size every minute to the canary config; low-risk.
jia: Uploading results to https://s3.internal/run-results/1782456789/ after tests complete. ETA ~4h.
oliver: Perfect. Thanks y'all. Please @me with direct links. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary pr-789 health check: memory usage across shards: [shard-1: 4.2GB, shard-2: 4.1GB, shard-3: 12.7GB (OOM)], sh-run: 1782459100.

kevin: If shard-3 is much higher, check node-level differences (kernel version, glibc, drivers). I've seen driver-level allocator differences bite before.
emma: I'll standby to revert if jia's runs show a clear regression.
jia: Test run finished. uploading artifacts now. Link: https://s3.internal/run-results/1782456789/results.zip
jia: Quick summary: pre-PR steady RSS ~5GB, pr-789 RSS grows ~2GB over 10mins with many small free failures in logs; pr-789 + bg-thread shows RSS growth limited to ~6GB. Perf shows hot path in `ephemeral_arena_alloc` called from `kv_cache_insert`.

oliver: that's very helpful. Sounds like PR 789 increases ephemeral churn and background jemalloc thread mitigates fragmentation. Emma, can we land a tiny patch to enable background thread by default on canary? Then we can evaluate long-term.
emma: I'll open a small config-only PR to set MALLOC_CONF for canary images. Drafting now.
sasha: Also may be worth adding a periodic compacting pass for ephemeral arenas when kv-cache reaches thresholds. Could be a follow-up.
kevin: Agree. For now, mitigation + revert plan is safe.
oliver: Closing loop — thanks everyone. I'll update the incident doc with links and action items.
